Our channel's explainers: editorial paper cut-outs over the speaker.
prompt: This is a section of a lecture by neuroscientist Lisa Genzel of Radboud University on how memory works. Turn it into an explainer for our channel: tighten out the pauses, put a title on it, introduce her with a name card when she's first on camera, call out the key points as she makes them, explain her main concepts visually instead of leaving it all to her talking, and caption the whole thing. The project is already set up in our channel's style.

checklist.description: A title-role overlay opens the video and holds at least 3 s
A lower third names her while she is first on camera (before 25 s) and holds at least 4 s
Two or more callouts, each up at least 3 s
Pauses came out: less footage than the 215 s source, but not gutted
No A-roll clip shorter than 1 s
Each kept segment keeps its own sound
A caption track with a real number of cues
At least one scene over the A roll, at least 4 s: a Group, or a drawn animation
No scene or plate hides the captions
A quote overlay uses her exact words
